minutes.headline: Commission approved a private water main extension without verifying the wetland flags shown on its own plan
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Conservation Commission heard a long slate of wetlands hearings, approving a privately-funded water main extension along Round/Parmenter/Ruth Streets (while explicitly declining to certify the wetland delineations shown), approving accessible parking and a rain garden at Hickory Hills, and approving a simplified landscape plan at 50 Pine Grove Road. Several other hearings, including a disputed house reconstruction at 18 Oakridge Road that stalled over encroachment into the 50-foot no-build zone, were continued to May 6, and the commission voted not to exercise its right of first refusal on a Lemonster/Lancaster Road property.

what_happened.line: The commission approved a private water main extension along Round/Parmenter/Ruth Streets while explicitly declining to certify the wetland flags shown on the applicant's own plan.
A resident had told the commission wetlands near his Ruth Street home were not flagged like others on that same project, given its size and proximity to Lake Shirley.
A disputed house reconstruction at 18 Oakridge Road stalled over the project's encroachment into the 50-foot wetland no-build zone and was continued to May 6.
The commission voted not to exercise the town's right of first refusal on a Lemonster/Lancaster Road property.
Hickory Hills' accessible parking and rain garden plan was approved on the condition of an asphalt surface and an agent-approved maintenance plan.

why_it_matters: The water main approval lets private construction proceed near Lake Shirley without the commission certifying where the wetlands actually are, a gap a resident raised directly at the hearing.
The town is passing on a chance to acquire the Lemonster/Lancaster Road parcel, which leaves its future use to whatever private sale follows.
A homeowner on Oakridge Road remains unable to finish a reconstruction project until the setback dispute is resolved at the May 6 hearing.
